newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Lloyds Bank to open Brazil asset management unit.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds Bank to open Brazil asset management unit.

text.p: Lloyds Bank do Brasil and its 50 percent owned associate Banco Multiplic announced plans to set up a fund management unit to be named Lloyds Asset Management (LAM), a company official said.
The new fund will begin operations at the beginning of November and will manage a portfolio of around $1.5 billion, said Lloyds Bank do Brasil president David Thomas.
"Our aim is to be one of the main asset management players in the market and offer a wide variety of product alternatives," Thomas said.
LAM will be 75 percent owned by Lloyds and 25 percent held by Multiplic.
The new fund will be based in Luxemburg and cater to the needs of individuals, foreign investors, corporations, institutional investors and foreign firms interested in investing in Brazil.

While the the bulk of the portfolio will initially be concentrated in the local fixed income markets, LAM will seek to offer investors a new range of alternatives in variable income instruments, Thomas said.
"Increasingly, the tendency will be to offer variable income products for sophisticated investors who understand the risk involved," he said.
Thomas said Lloyds Bank, which manages an international portfolio of $42 billion, has traditionally not had a very strong presence in the Brazilian fund management market.
However he said management of institutional portfolios, private banking and investment funds was the fastest growing area of the bank.
